### `FailFastPolicy` (sealed class)

An `IErrorPolicy` under which any filter fault halts the pipeline immediately. This is the safe default for stages where continuing past a failure would be wrong — e.g. a build step in a CI/CD-style pipeline.

**Remarks:**

Unlike `SkipAndContinuePolicy`, this policy requires no cooperation from the filter: letting an exception propagate out of a filter's `IAsyncEnumerable<TOut>` naturally halts the enclosing `await foreach`, which is exactly fail-fast semantics. Every `IFilter`2` implementation supports this policy, whether or not it implements `ISkipAndContinueCapable`.

#### `public static readonly FailFastPolicy Instance`

The shared, stateless instance of this policy.

#### `public bool ShouldContinue(Exception exception, ErrorContext context)`

---

### `IErrorPolicy` (interface)

Decides how a pipeline stage responds when a filter faults while processing an item. Modeled as an interface (not a closed enum) so additional policies — a retry-then-skip policy, for instance — can be added later without changing the core. See ADR-0006 for the full design rationale, including why this is a pipeline-level default with an optional per-filter override rather than a single pipeline-wide setting.

#### `bool ShouldContinue(Exception exception, ErrorContext context)`

Decides whether the pipeline should continue processing after a fault.

**Parameters:**

- `exception` — The exception the filter raised.
- `context` — Context about where the fault occurred.

**Returns:** `true` if the pipeline should skip the faulted item and continue; `false` if the pipeline should halt.

**Remarks:**

This method must be a pure decision — any side effect (logging, metrics) is the pipeline's responsibility via `IPipelineObserver`, not the policy's, so that observability happens consistently regardless of which policy is active.

### `SkipAndContinuePolicy` (sealed class)

An `IErrorPolicy` under which a filter fault is isolated to the item that caused it — the pipeline logs and skips that item (via `IPipelineObserver`, never silently) and continues processing subsequent items.

**Remarks:**

This policy can only be safely applied to a filter that implements `ISkipAndContinueCapable` — see the fault-isolation contract documented on `IFilter`2` for why. Attempting to apply it to a filter that hasn't opted in throws `NotSupportedException` when the pipeline is built, rather than risking undefined behavior from resuming a foreign enumerator after a fault.

#### `public static readonly SkipAndContinuePolicy Instance`

The shared, stateless instance of this policy.

### `IFilter<TIn, TOut>` (interface)

The core filter contract in the Pipes and Filters pattern. A filter consumes a stream of `TIn` items and produces a stream of `TOut` items.

**Type Parameters:**

- `TIn` — The type of items this filter consumes.
- `TOut` — The type of items this filter produces.

**Remarks:**

This is a Domain-layer contract: it has no dependency on how filters are composed, executed, or observed (those are Application-layer concerns — see `PipelineTemplate.Application.Composition`). It's the one thing every layer and every consumer agrees on.

The contract is intentionally cardinality-flexible: an implementation may yield zero, one, or many output items per input item (or per several input items), which is what lets it serve 1:1 transforms, filtering/sampling, windowing or aggregation (many:1), and fan-out-style expansion (1:many) — all without a different interface per shape. See ADR-0005 for the full reasoning behind choosing a streaming contract over a synchronous or item-at-a-time asynchronous one.

**Fault-isolation contract for implementers:** the pipeline's error-handling policy (ADR-0006) can only safely apply `SkipAndContinue` semantics to a filter that isolates its own per-item faults internally (catching around the processing of one logical unit of work and continuing its own iteration) rather than letting an exception escape from advancing its output enumerator. See `ISkipAndContinueCapable` for how a filter opts into this, and `PipelineTemplate.Application.Filters.TransformFilter<TIn, TOut>` for the supported-out-of-the-box way to get this right for ordinary one-in-one-out filters.

#### `IAsyncEnumerable<TOut> ProcessAsync(IAsyncEnumerable<TIn> input, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default(CancellationToken))`

Processes a stream of input items, producing a stream of output items.

**Parameters:**

- `input` — The upstream sequence of items to process.
- `cancellationToken` — A token to cancel processing.

**Returns:** The resulting sequence of output items.

---

### `ISkipAndContinueCapable` (interface)

Implemented by filters that isolate their own per-item faults internally and can therefore safely support the `SkipAndContinuePolicy` error policy.

**Remarks:**

`PipelineTemplate.Application.Filters.TransformFilter<TIn, TOut>` implements this automatically for the common one-in-one-out case. A hand-written filter that produces or consumes multiple items per logical unit of work (windowing, aggregation, fan-out) can implement this too, but only if it genuinely catches and isolates faults around its own per-item work — see the fault-isolation contract documented on `IFilter`2`.

A filter that does **not** implement this interface can still be used in a pipeline, but only under a `FailFastPolicy` — the pipeline builder rejects an attempt to apply `SkipAndContinuePolicy` to a filter that hasn't opted in, rather than risking undefined behavior from resuming a foreign enumerator after a fault.

#### `void Configure(IErrorPolicy policy, IPipelineObserver observer, string stageName)`

Called by the pipeline builder when this filter is added to a pipeline, supplying the resolved error policy, observer, and a display name for observability and exception messages.

---

### `IPipelineObserver` (interface)

Receives per-filter telemetry as a pipeline runs — throughput, latency, and error rate per stage, per `non-functional-requirements.md` §6. Implementations are expected to be cheap and non-blocking; the pipeline calls these hooks inline on the processing path.

**Remarks:**

This is a Domain-layer port: the contract every layer agrees on. Concrete adapters belong outward — `PipelineTemplate.Application.Observability.NullPipelineObserver` is the default, dependency-free no-op; a real backend (OpenTelemetry, Serilog, etc.) would be an Infrastructure-layer adapter, supplied by the consumer via `PipelineBuilder.WithObserver(...)`.

#### `void OnItemProcessed(string stageName, TimeSpan duration)`

Called after a filter successfully produces an item.

#### `void OnItemFaulted(string stageName, Exception exception, bool willContinue)`

Called whenever a filter faults while processing an item, regardless of which error policy is active — this is what makes `SkipAndContinuePolicy` observable rather than a silent data sink.

**Parameters:**

- `stageName` — The display name of the stage that faulted.
- `exception` — The exception the filter raised.
- `willContinue` — Whether the active policy decided the pipeline should continue past this fault.

### `Pipeline` (class)

Entry point for composing a new pipeline. See ADR-0007 for the composition-style decision and ADR-0006 for the default error-policy model.

#### `public static PipelineBuilder<TIn, TIn> Create<TIn>(IErrorPolicy defaultErrorPolicy = null, IPipelineObserver observer = null)`

Starts building a new pipeline accepting `TIn` as input.

**Parameters:**

- `defaultErrorPolicy` — The pipeline-wide default error policy, overridable per filter via `AddFilter``1`. Defaults to `FailFastPolicy` if not supplied.
- `observer` — The observer to report per-filter telemetry to. Defaults to `NullPipelineObserver` (no-op) if not supplied.

### `PipelineBuilder<TIn, TCurrent>` (sealed class)

A strongly-typed, immutable fluent builder for composing a linear chain of filters into a runnable `Pipeline`2`. See ADR-0007 for why this is code-first rather than declarative/config-driven, and ADR-0004 for why v1 composition is linear only.

**Type Parameters:**

- `TIn` — The type the overall pipeline accepts as input.
- `TCurrent` — The type the pipeline currently produces — i.e. what the next `AddFilter``1` call must accept.

**Remarks:**

Each call to `AddFilter``1` returns a new builder rather than mutating this one, so a partially-built pipeline can be safely reused as a starting point for more than one variant. This is Application-layer orchestration: it composes Domain-layer `IFilter`2` and `IErrorPolicy` contracts into a runnable use case, but defines none of the pattern's core rules itself.

#### `public PipelineBuilder<TIn, TNext> AddFilter<TNext>(IFilter<TCurrent, TNext> filter, IErrorPolicy errorPolicy = null, string stageName = null)`

Adds a filter to the pipeline. The pipeline's default error policy applies unless `errorPolicy` overrides it for this stage — see ADR-0006. The stage's display name (used in exception messages and reported to the observer) defaults to the filter's type name; supply `stageName` to override it — useful when the same filter type is reused for several differently-named stages in one pipeline.

**Throws:**

- `NotSupportedException` — The resolved policy is `SkipAndContinuePolicy` and `filter` does not implement `ISkipAndContinueCapable` — see the fault-isolation contract on `IFilter`2` for why this can't be done safely for an arbitrary filter.

#### `public PipelineBuilder<TIn, TNext> AddFilter<TNext>(Func<TCurrent, TNext> transform, IErrorPolicy errorPolicy = null, string stageName = null)`

Adds a synchronous 1:1 transform as a filter, via `DelegateTransformFilter`2`.

#### `public PipelineBuilder<TIn, TNext> AddFilter<TNext>(Func<TCurrent, CancellationToken, Task<TNext>> transform, IErrorPolicy errorPolicy = null, string stageName = null)`

Adds an asynchronous 1:1 transform as a filter, via `DelegateTransformFilter`2`.

#### `public PipelineBuilder<TIn, TCurrent> WithDefaultErrorPolicy(IErrorPolicy policy)`

Returns a builder with a new default error policy, applied to filters added after this call. Does not change stages already added.

#### `public PipelineBuilder<TIn, TCurrent> WithObserver(IPipelineObserver observer)`

Returns a builder with a new observer, applied to filters added after this call.

### `TransformFilter<TIn, TOut>` (abstract class)

A base class for ordinary one-in-one-out filters, so authoring a simple transform doesn't require hand-writing an async iterator against the Domain layer's streaming `IFilter`2` contract directly. This is the ADR-0005 developer-experience mitigation, and it is also the supported, safe way to get per-item `SkipAndContinuePolicy` semantics: this class isolates faults around its own per-item work — catching around the call to `TransformAsync` and continuing its own `await foreach` over the upstream input — which never requires resuming a foreign enumerator after an exception.

**Type Parameters:**

- `TIn` — The type of items consumed.
- `TOut` — The type of items produced.

**Remarks:**

This lives in the Application layer, not Domain, because it orchestrates policy application and observability reporting around the pure `IFilter`2` contract — that orchestration is a use-case-level concern, not a rule of the pattern itself.

#### `protected abstract Task<TOut> TransformAsync(TIn item, CancellationToken cancellationToken)`

Transforms a single input item into a single output item.

### `NullPipelineObserver` (sealed class)

An `IPipelineObserver` that does nothing. The default observer for a pipeline that hasn't been given one — see NFR §8 ("observability is opt-out, not omitted": the hooks always exist, but cost nothing until a real observer is supplied). A real, technology-specific observer (OpenTelemetry, Serilog, etc.) belongs in the Infrastructure layer, not here.
